editorial.headline: General Goods by Road: The Business Behind the Load
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers general goods transport by motor vehicle—open nationally to full foreign ownership, with no Bali moratorium block identified at the large-business risk level.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is the operation of general goods transport by motor vehicle. It is the business of moving freight that may comprise more than one type of goods, using vehicles such as trucks, pick-ups, open-bed vehicles and enclosed box vehicles. The emphasis is operational: the enterprise is organised around carrying goods on the road. The record expressly accommodates more than one type of goods, giving the activity a general-goods character rather than limiting it to one cargo type.

Registration is open at every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That is a broad scale profile. The classification does not confine the activity to a small operator or reserve it for a large one. Its defining work remains goods transportation with motor vehicles, and its listed examples give the scope a practical physical shape: trucks, pick-ups, open beds and closed box bodies. The activity is therefore best understood as a road-freight operation whose business is the movement of general goods.

Nationally, the foreign-investment position is straightforward. The PMA status is TERBUKA, and the recorded maximum foreign ownership is 100%. For a foreign-owned company, that means the national ceiling permits full foreign ownership for this activity. The cited basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Here, openness is not merely a broad description: it sits alongside a stated ownership ceiling, giving the national position a definite reading for a business considering PMA registration.

Bali requires a separate reading, but it does not reverse the national result. The Bali assessment is recorded as OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, and this activity is not flagged as blocked for PMA registration under the province’s moratorium. The record gives the reason: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is medium-high/high, so the moratorium does not block it. Bali’s stated rule is a permanent, island-wide PMA block for Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. That province-wide rule is real, yet this activity falls outside the recorded block. The honest picture is therefore clear: full foreign ownership is nationally permitted, and the Bali moratorium is not the recorded barrier to PMA registration for this activity.
